description: The rolling worker upgrade as it happens: which versions the nodes are on, where {{.WorkloadName}} is running, which node is cordoned, and whether availability held.

options.content: Roll one worker at a time. **Nodes by kubelet version** should show a second version appear and then take over as each node is replaced — if two versions persist, the roll is unfinished. **{{.WorkloadName}} pods per node** must never collapse to a single node: that means the next drain takes the whole app down. **Success rate** is the grade.

panels.title: Nodes by kubelet version (the roll in progress)
panels.description: Each node replaced onto the target image moves from the old series to the new one. Two series at once is a roll mid-flight; one series is a finished roll.

panels.title: {{.WorkloadName}} pods per node (spread must survive the roll)
panels.description: If this drops to a single node, the PodDisruptionBudget is the only thing standing between the next drain and a full outage.

panels.title: Cordoned nodes (1 = SchedulingDisabled)
panels.description: Should rise to 1 while you drain a node and return to 0 once its replacement joins. A node left at 1 is a roll you did not finish.

panels.title: PodDisruptionBudget: healthy pods vs disruptions allowed
panels.description: When 'disruptions allowed' sits at 0 the PDB is actively blocking an eviction — that pause is the drill working.

panels.title: {{.WorkloadName}} success rate across the upgrade (the grade)
panels.description: The scenario passes at >= 0.99 over a 10m window. Brief dips as a node cycles are expected; a sustained drop means a drain took the last healthy replica.

panels.title: Request rate reaching {{.WorkloadName}} (the grade is meaningless without load)
panels.description: A drain evicts the k6 traffic Job and it does not restart itself. If this flatlines, restart traffic before grading.

title: Cluster Upgrade Drill
